ta-01.note: 눈 means eye on your face (눈이 커요) and also snow falling from the sky (눈이 와요). Context tells the meaning.
배 means stomach (배가 아파요), the pear fruit (달콤한 배), or a ship on water (배를 타요).
다리 means a leg on your body (다리가 길어요) and also a bridge across water (다리를 건너요).

ta-02.note: 작다 means small in physical size (가방이 작아요), while 적다 means small in quantity or number (학생 수가 적어요). Do not mix them up.
빠르다 is an adjective meaning to be fast (비행기가 빨라요), while 빨리 is an adverb meaning quickly (빨리 오세요).
Opposites. 시작하다 means to begin an action (수업을 시작해요), while 끝나다 means to finish or end (영화가 끝나요).

ta-03.note: Both mean all or everyone. 다 is an everyday adverb (숙제를 다 했어요), while 모두 can be used as a noun or adverb (친구가 모두 왔어요).
Opposites. 많이 means a lot or much (밥을 많이 먹어요), while 조금 (or 좀) means a little (조금 기다리세요).
가장 means the most or best before adjectives (가장 좋아요), and also means the head of a family (우리 집의 가장).

ta-04.note: Both mean the most or best. 가장 is native Korean (가장 커요), while 제일 is Sino-Korean and very common in conversation (제일 좋아요).
Opposites. 높다 means high or tall (산이 높아요), while 낮다 means low (책상이 낮아요).
만 is the number ten thousand (만 원), and also a particle meaning only attached to nouns (물만 마셔요).

ta-05.note: 약 means medicine (약을 먹어요), and also means approximately or about before numbers (약 10분 걸려요).
반 means half (한 시 반, 반 개), and also means a class group at school (우리 반 친구).
셋 is the native number three used with counters (사과 세 개), while 삼 is the Sino-Korean number used for dates and minutes (3월, 삼십 분).

ta-06.note: 열 is the native Korean number ten (열 명), and also means a fever or body heat (열이 나요).
안 means inside (가방 안), and also the negative word not placed before verbs (안 가요, 안 먹어요).
셋 changes to 세 before a counter or noun (세 살, 세 개). Use 셋 when counting numbers by themselves (하나, 둘, 셋).

ta-07.note: Both mean birthday. 생일 is the standard everyday word (친구 생일), while 생신 is the honorific word used for elders (할머니 생신).
Opposites. 앞 means front (학교 앞), while 뒤 means behind or back (집 뒤). They also describe time order (앞으로 vs 뒤에).
Opposites. 가깝다 means near or close (역에서 가까워요), while 멀다 means far away (회사가 멀어요).

ta-08.note: Korean uses different verbs for clothes. 입다 is for body garments like shirts and pants (옷을 입어요), while 신다 is for footwear on feet (신발을 신어요).
Both are shoes. 구두 refers to dress shoes or formal leather shoes (구두를 신어요), while 운동화 refers to sneakers or sports shoes (운동화를 신어요).
원 is the currency unit of Korea (천 원), and also means a geometric circle (동그란 원).

ta-09.note: Both mean to sleep. 자다 is the standard verb (동생이 자요), while 주무시다 is the respectful honorific verb for elders (부모님이 주무세요).
빌리다 means to borrow from someone (도서관에서 책을 빌려요), while 빌려주다 means to lend to someone (친구에게 우산을 빌려줘요).
들다 has several common uses: to hold or carry in hand (가방을 들어요), or to like (마음에 들어요), or to cost money (돈이 들어요).

ta-10.note: 다녀오다 means to go somewhere and come back (학교에 다녀왔어요), while 돌아오다 emphasizes returning back to the starting place (집으로 돌아와요).
걷다 means to walk on foot (공원을 걸어요), and also to roll up sleeves or collect laundry (빨래를 걷어요).
Both mean a meal. 밥 is the everyday Korean word (밥을 먹어요), while 식사 is the formal Sino-Korean word (맛있게 식사하세요).
